static_traits.name: Chen Kai
static_traits.family_status: Has two siblings, keeps a dog
static_traits.social_status: Can communicate with two siblings, but has not yet discussed this issue with them; other social circumstances not disclosed
static_traits.medical_history: No history of psychotherapy, no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear thinking and expression, able to concretely describe events and feelings; relatively high cooperation; obvious tendencies toward catastrophizing, overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking, and jumping to conclusions

basic_info.main_problem: Since the dog had an accident at home, I keep feeling intense frustration and despair, believing it will never be fully toilet trained.
basic_info.core_demands: When frustration and despair started affecting my overall well-being and daily life, I decided to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent/not suited to raising a dog

special_situations.event: The dog had an accident on the carpet today
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an accident happens in one training session, the training is a failure and I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Intensifying the use of various training methods and cleaning procedures, and trying stricter routines
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will never learn to use the toilet

special_situations.event: Being busy or distracted leading to not taking the dog out on time, followed by indoor accidents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot fully control every variable, any mistake proves I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Blaming and negating oneself, while setting more reminders and strengthening the schedule to avoid further mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault, I am just incompetent

special_situations.event: Within one week there were both indoor accidents and successful outdoor toileting
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative events matter more; positive progress does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores successes, focuses on the negative, and loudly scolds after accidents, then feels guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These small successes do not count at all; I am forever cleaning up messes

special_situations.event: After every indoor accident, immediately draws a negative conclusion about training as a whole
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Magnifies negative conclusions, questions whether one should keep a dog
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will never be properly toilet trained

core_conflict.wish: Longs to become a competent dog owner in control, and to be affirmed as capable
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being proven incompetent and a failure, worrying about losing control and regretting getting the dog
defense_goal: Preventing failure by strictly controlling the schedule and doubling down on training; staying vigilant through self-denial to avoid further mistakes

object_relations.object_representation: A trainee (dog) that is hard to control and frequently causes trouble

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the dog has an accident at home
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Immediately equates one accident with permanent training failure, and attributes the failure to myself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use self-denial statements, in a low tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'It is all my fault'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor guides him to focus on positive progress or suggests recording successes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing positive evidence is unimportant or insufficient to change the conclusion, holding onto the negative judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Offering seemingly rational interpretations to negate positive evidence, emphasizing 'these successes mean nothing' in a calm but firm tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the schedule is disrupted and being unable to take the dog out on time leads to accidents
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treating uncontrollable external disruptions as catastrophes, and displacing emotions onto the dog
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Raises his voice to scold the dog, emotionally intense; then expresses guilt and self-blame.

manifestations: Feeling hopeless about training, questioning whether suited to raising a dog, with positive progress overshadowed by negative events
outcomes: Daily routine and cleaning habits affected

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Attributing training mistakes entirely to oneself
Difficulty accepting small successes and progress

exception_events.target_problem: When the dog has an accident at home, the client typically catastrophizes and jumps to conclusions, generating intense frustration and despair that ruin the day's mood and schedule
exception_events.unique_outcome: While keeping to a strict routine (setting reminders and taking the dog out on time), the dog did its toileting outdoors, the client gave timely rewards and praise, the mood was relatively stable, and stress was clearly lower
exception_events.reason: Different approach: setting reminders and keeping more consistent outing times; different support: using positive reinforcement (rewards and praise); different situation: a more controllable rhythm with fewer accidents

positive_force: Willing to try various training methods and cleaning routines
Able to maintain and benefit from a stricter schedule (self-management ability)
Has two siblings who can be potential support resources
Willing to conduct reality testing and record small successes, trying to adjust cognition
negative_force: High stress; tends to ignore positive evidence (focuses only on the negative)

target_behavior.behavior: When the dog has an indoor accident, shows intense anger and self-blame and shouts loudly
antecedent: Finding a mess right after getting up in the morning before starting the daily routine
Distraction or busyness leading to not taking the dog out on time yet
Seeing stains and odors that need cleaning
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing one accident and overgeneralizing it as permanent training failure, then attributing the failure to one's own incompetence
target_behavior.function: Releasing inner tension and anxiety to gain a brief sense of control, while avoiding helplessness and the sense of failure
target_behavior.consequence: Intensifying stress and despair, ruining the day's mood and daily routine, with negative interactions unhelpful to training outcomes
